newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded, diesel prices steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded, diesel prices steady.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline and diesel prices were steady on Monday as firming differentials offset weaker futures prices, traders said.
Bidders emerged early Monday into a market with few sellers, driving differentials higher in Chicago and Group Three would firm against the weakening heating oil futures.
"Differentials should be much stronger by Wednesday," one Chicago-area trader said. "There are bidders out there, but no sellers."
Traders saw continued downward pressure on prices heading into the final weeks of the year. "The whole market appears soft," a Group Three trader said.

Prices in the Midwest had moved higher on agricultural demand and autumn gasoline demand, but with those drivers out of the market and refinery output back at normal levels, a seasonal correction was seen underway.
"We're going back to normal numbers and normal cracks spreads for this time of year," one trader active in both markets said. "We've been too high for two months."
High sulphur diesel eased to 7.0 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago and 6.50 cents a gallon under the print in Group Three, traders said.
Prompt unleaded gasoline was bid 2.0 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago and 3.25 cents under in Grour Three, with later deliveries 0.50 cent weaker in both markets.
